walkthroughs.body_html:
Area of Study 2: The Concerto Through Time — a core area of GCSE Music.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Area of Study 2: The Concerto Through Time brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Area of Study 2: The Concerto Through Time.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: A waltz is in which time?
What does the time signature 6/8 indicate?
options: Two beats per bar, each beat divided into three (compound duple).
Six beats per bar, all equal in stress.
Dorian has no sharps or flats at all.
A piece six bars long.

mcqs.q: How does D Dorian differ from D minor?
options: A piece six bars long.
They are the same scale.
Dorian has a raised 6th (B natural) compared to natural minor.
Dorian has no sharps or flats at all.

mcqs.q: How does a harmonic minor scale differ from a natural minor?
options: The seventh degree is raised by a semitone (creating a leading note).
Dorian has no sharps or flats at all.
All notes are raised by a semitone.
It has only five notes.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Simple time”?
options: Two numbers at the start of a piece: top = beats per bar, bottom = note value of beat.
Each beat divides into two (e.g., 2/4, 3/4, 4/4).
Three crotchet beats per bar; used for waltzes.
Each beat divides into three (e.g., 6/8, 9/8, 12/8).

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “4/4 (common time)”?
options: Six quaver beats grouped in twos; a swaying, dance-like feel.
Each beat divides into two (e.g., 2/4, 3/4, 4/4).
Four crotchet beats per bar; the most common signature in popular music.
Each beat divides into three (e.g., 6/8, 9/8, 12/8).

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Compound time”?
options: Each beat divides into three (e.g., 6/8, 9/8, 12/8).
Each beat divides into two (e.g., 2/4, 3/4, 4/4).
Six quaver beats grouped in twos; a swaying, dance-like feel.
Four crotchet beats per bar; the most common signature in popular music.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “6/8 (compound duple)”?
options: Six quaver beats grouped in twos; a swaying, dance-like feel.
Four crotchet beats per bar; the most common signature in popular music.
Two numbers at the start of a piece: top = beats per bar, bottom = note value of beat.
Three crotchet beats per bar; used for waltzes.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “3/4 (waltz time)”?
options: Six quaver beats grouped in twos; a swaying, dance-like feel.
Each beat divides into three (e.g., 6/8, 9/8, 12/8).
Four crotchet beats per bar; the most common signature in popular music.
Three crotchet beats per bar; used for waltzes.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Time signature”?
options: Six quaver beats grouped in twos; a swaying, dance-like feel.
Each beat divides into three (e.g., 6/8, 9/8, 12/8).
Three crotchet beats per bar; used for waltzes.
Two numbers at the start of a piece: top = beats per bar, bottom = note value of beat.
